title: Earthquake-induced environmental impacts for residential Italian buildings: Consequence models and risk assessment
publication: Journal of Building Engineering 84 (2024), 108149; online 21 November 2023
reading_coverage: Printed pages 1–20: sections 1–9, all extracted tables, Appendix and references. Figure captions and accompanying interpretation read; images not visually inspected by this agent.
source_version: Published CC BY 4.0 article uploaded by author Karim Aljawhari on 23 January 2024
local_pdf_status: Parent handles browser download; this agent's publisher, ResearchGate and thesis PDF HTTP requests returned403
scope_reason: Uncertain seismic damage, repair quantities and repairability map to embodied-carbon distributions. Waste recycling is fixed at90%; uncertain recovery yield, quality loss, contamination and secondary-material substitution credits are not modeled.

system_boundary.appendix_caution: Worked example p18 assumes100% landfill and zero construction waste, unlike main models

propagation_steps.input: EPD carbon-factor variability and uniform wall dimensions
propagation_steps.mapping: 10000 Monte Carlo samples; repair action geometry to material quantities; multiply factors; add demolition/disposal; normalize by wall area
propagation_steps.output: Lognormal component repair-carbon median and dispersion by DS

propagation_steps.input: Uniform room/bathroom dimensions and bathroom area share plus sampled carbon factors
propagation_steps.mapping: 10000 samples through weighted ideal-room services inventory
propagation_steps.output: Services carbon-per-area lognormal median and dispersion

propagation_steps.input: Uniform beam/column/floor/span geometry and carbon-factor variation
propagation_steps.mapping: 10000 Monte Carlo samples of DS-specific repair actions and material quantities

propagation_steps.input: Hazard-consistent seismic response samples, component fragilities and carbon consequences
propagation_steps.mapping: FEMA P-58/PACT samples EDPs, damage states and consequences; aggregates components and repairability/replacement branches;1000 realizations per intensity
propagation_steps.output: Building-carbon realizations, annual exceedance curves and expected annual environmental loss

propagation_steps.input: PACT carbon realizations and associated maximum interstorey drifts
propagation_steps.mapping: Condition on global DS via drift thresholds; normalize by replacement carbon; construct ECDF and fit Beta distribution; combine with fragility/hazard
propagation_steps.output: Portable DS-conditioned carbon ratio distributions, means/CoVs, vulnerability means and16th/84th fractiles

uncertain_inputs.carbon_factors: EPDItaly and European references; more than60 manufacturers,230 product classes; means/SD Table1; sampling distribution family not clearly named in text
uncertain_inputs.infill_geometry: Uniform h2.50–2.75m,l4–5m; fixed window0.90×1.5m and door1.20×2.20m
uncertain_inputs.services_geometry: Room dimensions uniform3–4.5m; bathroom minimum dimension1.7–3m; bathroom area3.5–5m2; area weight0.05–0.10
uncertain_inputs.structural_geometry: Beam width0.25–0.40m/depth0.35–0.60m; column size0.30–0.60m; floor height3–4.5m; span4–6m, all uniform
uncertain_inputs.seismic_hazard: 14 intensity stripes,return periods30–9975years,L'Aquila; avgSa over10 periods0.2T1–1.5T1
uncertain_inputs.data_quality: Published Eq4: sqrt(beta_calculated² + 0.25), no square on 0.25; visually verified by parent in publisher HTML. This implies beta>=0.5, inconsistent with Table3 values below0.5. Intended implementation unresolved; no correction assumed.

dependence_assumptions: Services damage correlated with infill state and uses same fragilities (pp7,12)
Component damage and resulting carbon within performance groups assumed uncorrelated (p12)
Cost/carbon correlation analysis shares demand and damage realizations; not independent empirical validation (pp16–17)

repairability.threshold: Replacement at60% of replacement value; collapse and residual-drift repairability also considered
repairability.beta_ratio_exclusion: Collapse and excessive residual-drift realizations excluded from fitted DS-conditioned ratios, though included in full PACT assessment

example_outputs.annual_risk: Section6.2 p13:3-High EAL57% lower than3-Pre;8-Low16% lower than8-Pre
example_outputs.service_life: 50-year averages: high-code about16% and pre-code about27% of initial construction carbon in results text; conclusion says close to30% pre-code,24% low-code. Do not turn rounded/contextual values into universal constant.

validation.surrogate_agreement: Illustrated mean deviations no more than5% at a few intensity stripes;16th/84th fractiles also comparable
validation.goodness_of_fit: Most DS2–4 Beta fits non-rejected at5%; some require2–4%. Most DS1 fail at5% and only non-rejected at much lower alpha. Lowering alpha is weaker evidence, not a correction.

cost_proxy.finding: Normalized cost/carbon rho0.99 above loss ratio0.15; shared physical damage drives association
cost_proxy.limitations: Cost includes labor/technical/shoring items omitted from carbon; DS1 proxy discrepancy21–31%,DS2 about9%,DS3–4 under4%; overestimates annual risk dominated by frequent light damage

limitations: Nine regular RC archetypes and single seismic setting
Detailed structural response/hazard/fragility information inherited from separate paper10.1016/j.soildyn.2023.107979
US fragilities substituted for unavailable Italian low/high-code component data
Carbon-factor probability family and correlations not clearly specified
Fixed recycling, treatment, replacement and threshold assumptions
Partial lifecycle boundary and transportation omission
No recovered-component quality, market or salvage-yield uncertainty model
No actual digital twin; retrofit optimization left for future work
Published Eq4 implies beta>=0.5 but Table3 reports lower values; parent visually confirmed HTML inconsistency; actual dispersion-adjustment implementation unresolved
reviewer_method: Assistant complete available full-article text reading; no independent human review
